sources.title: David P. Woodruff, Sketching as a Tool for Numerical Linear Algebra
sources.locator: Complete 157-page monograph PDF fetched and extracted. Inspected §2.1 Definitions 1–2, Lemma 5 and Theorem 6; §2.4 Definition 16, Theorem 17 and its proof; §2.5 Definition 20 and Theorem 21 proof; and §2.6, printed pp. 34–35, on QR from SA and the resulting condition-number bound. The full argument was compared with the local proofs; no omitted matrix-concentration proof is imported.
sources.reading_verification: The full PDF was downloaded and extracted with mutool. The complete cited sections and each named theorem proof listed above were inspected; Theorem 17's matrix-Chernoff application is independently reconstructed from the repository's proved matrix-Bernstein item.

contents.name: §2.1, Definitions 1–2: squared-norm embedding and the fixed-subspace oblivious quantifier
contents.reason: The local definition fixes the squared-norm convention and states explicitly that the random draw succeeds for each subspace fixed before sampling, not simultaneously for every subspace.

contents.name: §2.1, Lemma 5: finite net on the unit sphere of the embedded subspace
contents.reason: The real-dimensional volume argument and operator-net transfer motivate the local Hermitian proof; the local item extends the transfer explicitly to complex coordinates and states the exact 1/4-net constants it uses.

contents.name: §2.1, Theorem 4 and Theorem 6: Gaussian vector tails and Gaussian subspace-embedding dimension
contents.locator: §2.1, printed pp. 11–14, Theorems 4 and 6 and their preceding net argument
contents.reason: The local theorem supplies the scalar real and normalized-complex moment-generating-function tails, a complete net union bound, the fixed-subspace quantifier, and the dimension-dependent operator-norm transfer.

contents.name: §2.4, Definition 16: with-replacement leverage sampling and row rescaling
contents.reason: The local algorithm records independent sampling with replacement, the exact 1/sqrt(m pi_i) scaling, the approximate leverage lower bound, and zero-probability zero-leverage rows.

contents.name: §2.4, Theorem 17: leverage sampling embeds an orthonormal column space
contents.locator: §2.4, printed pp. 27–29, Theorem 17 and complete proof
contents.reason: The local proof verifies the rank-one sample mean and variance, invokes the complete published matrix-Bernstein supplier, and derives both the general log(2d/delta) bound and the requested log(d/delta) form for delta at most one half.

contents.name: §2.5, Definitions 20 and Theorem 21: sketch-and-solve on span(A,b)
contents.locator: §2.5, printed pp. 30–32, Definition 20 and the complete proof of Theorem 21
contents.reason: The local statement uses the precise residual subspace span(Ran(A),b), proves both objective sandwiches and keeps the computed solve's exact-arithmetic condition explicit.

contents.name: §2.6, machine-precision regression: QR of SA as a right preconditioner
contents.locator: §2.6, printed pp. 34–35, paragraph beginning 'Suppose we apply a sparse subspace embedding matrix S to A'
contents.reason: The local proof derives the singular-value interval for AR^{-1} directly from an exact reduced QR and the embedding inequalities, and keeps all factorization-failure and finite-precision claims outside that exact result.

contents.name: §2.1 and §2.6, SRHT and sparse-embedding variants not commissioned as algorithms here
contents.reason: The controlling design calls SRHT and sparse CountSketch optional, each requiring its own dimension or coherence theorem. This batch does not promise either variant; the FFT page remains a declared page-context dependency only.

sources.title: Michael W. Mahoney, Randomized Algorithms for Matrices and Data
sources.locator: Complete 54-page monograph PDF fetched and extracted. Inspected §4.1, printed pp. 19–20, on leverage scores and basis invariance; §4.2, printed pp. 21–22, on row sampling, rescaling and least-squares residuals; and §4.3, printed pp. 22–23, on deterministic conditions for sketching and preconditioning.
sources.reading_verification: The complete PDF was downloaded and extracted with mutool. The full text of §§4.1–4.3, including the row-sampling derivation and the structural preconditioning discussion, was inspected.

contents.name: §4.1: leverage as the row norm of any orthonormal basis, basis invariance and coherence
contents.reason: The local lemma proves basis invariance, the dimension sum, the zero-row criterion and the upper bound by one from the orthogonal projection.

contents.name: §4.2: exact leverage sampling, rescaling and sampled least-squares objective
contents.reason: The local algorithm fixes the sampling-with-replacement and inverse-square-root scaling conventions and states the approximate-probability lower bound explicitly.

contents.name: §4.2: relative residual guarantee for the sampled least-squares solution
contents.locator: §4.2, printed pp. 21–22, equation (11) and surrounding discussion
contents.reason: This is an independent application-level comparison; the local theorem proves its stronger subspace-embedding guarantee with explicit failure probability and constants rather than importing the source's asymptotic claim.

contents.name: §4.3: deterministic geometric conditions sufficient for sketch-and-solve regression
contents.reason: The source separates embedding of the design column space from control of the residual direction; the local proof states and proves the sufficient span(A,b) hypothesis directly.

contents.name: §4.3–§4.4: right preconditioning and the role of an embedded QR factor
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the exact singular-value bounds for AP_S from QR and the subspace-embedding inequality without importing a finite-precision solver claim.

sources.title: Joel A. Tropp, An Introduction to Matrix Concentration Inequalities
sources.locator: Complete 163-page monograph PDF fetched and extracted. Inspected Theorem 6.1.1 in §6.1.1 and the complete Hermitian proof in §§6.6.1–6.6.5, including Lemma 6.6.2, the independent-sum variance calculation, the tail optimization and Hermitian dilation.
sources.reading_verification: The complete PDF was downloaded and extracted with mutool. The theorem statement and its full matrix-mgf/Lieb proof route through the rectangular dilation were inspected. The current library's locally proved Golden–Thompson route is used as the mathematical supplier; the monograph is not substituted for that proof.

contents.name: Theorem 6.1.1: bounded independent matrix Bernstein concentration
contents.reason: The repository already contains a complete local proof of the Hermitian operator-norm form, with exact centeredness, norm and variance hypotheses.

contents.name: Lemma 6.6.2 and §§6.6.3–6.6.4: matrix mgf, independent-sum tail and Chernoff optimization
contents.reason: The consumer proof verifies the supplier's exact norm and variance bounds for each rescaled leverage sample and performs the sample-size conversion locally; it uses no unproved concentration citation.

contents.name: §6.6.5: Hermitian dilation for general rectangular matrix sums
contents.reason: The leverage-score summands in this batch are already Hermitian d-by-d matrices, so the rectangular dilation branch is unnecessary for every assigned claim.
